seo.title: Pilates FAQ Limassol | First Class, What to Wear, Parking | KLUB
seo.description: Everything you need to know before your first Pilates class in Limassol: what to wear, grip socks, class sizes, pregnancy Pilates, back pain, parking and more.

hero.heading: Your Questions, Answered
hero.intro: Everything people ask before their first class — and a few things they wish they'd asked.

still.heading: Still have questions?
still.text: Message us — we typically reply within 30 minutes during business hours.

items.q: What is reformer Pilates?
items.a: Reformer Pilates is practiced on a machine with a sliding carriage, springs and straps. The springs add resistance and support, making exercises both harder and safer than mat work alone. It builds strength, flexibility and control — and it is genuinely fun.

items.q: Do I need any experience to start?
items.a: None at all. Our Reformer Fundamentals class is built for complete beginners — you will learn the machine from zero with a maximum of six people in the room.

items.q: What should I wear?
items.a: Comfortable leggings or shorts and a fitted top that lets your instructor see your alignment. Avoid anything with zips that could scratch the equipment.

items.q: Do I need grip socks?
items.a: Yes — grip socks are required in all classes for hygiene and safety. Bring your own or buy a pair at reception.

items.q: What should I bring?
items.a: Just yourself, grip socks and a bottle of water. Everything else is provided.

items.q: What happens if I arrive late?
items.a: Doors close 10 minutes after class starts — the warm-up matters for safety. If you miss the window, we will happily help you rebook.

items.q: Is Pilates a good workout, or is it too gentle?
items.a: Both, depending on the class. Fundamentals is measured and controlled; Power will challenge experienced athletes. Every class is a genuine full-body workout — expect to feel muscles you forgot you had.

items.q: How quickly will I notice results?
items.a: Most people feel a difference in posture and core awareness within a few sessions, and see visible change with two to three classes a week over a couple of months. Consistency beats intensity.

items.q: How big are the classes?
items.a: Maximum six people. Small enough that your instructor sees and corrects every rep.

items.q: How long is a class?
items.a: All group classes and private sessions are 50 minutes.

items.q: Can I book a private 1-to-1 session?
items.a: Yes — we are one of the few city-center studios offering true private sessions. They run by appointment and start from €70 per session in packs.

items.q: How do I book?
items.a: Online booking opens shortly before we launch in September 2026. Until then, join the founding member list for first access, or message us and we will reserve your spot personally.

items.q: What's the cancellation policy?
items.a: Cancel at least 12 hours before class and your credit returns to your account automatically. Later than that, the class is charged — the spot was held for you in a room of six.

items.q: Is there a waitlist for full classes?
items.a: Yes. If a class is full, join the waitlist and you will be notified automatically the moment a spot opens.

items.q: Where exactly is the studio?
items.a: We are in Limassol city center. The exact street address is being announced with our opening — join the founding member list or follow @klubstudios and you will be the first to know.

items.q: Is there parking nearby?
items.a: Yes — public parking is available within a short walk of the studio. We will publish a simple parking guide before opening day.

items.q: Can I reach you by public transport?
items.a: The studio is centrally located and well served by city bus routes. Exact stop details will be published with our address.

items.q: Do you have changing rooms?
items.a: Yes — changing facilities are available, so a lunchtime class between meetings is absolutely doable.

items.q: Can I store my things during class?
items.a: Yes, there is space for your belongings inside the studio, always within sight.

items.q: Is the studio air-conditioned?
items.a: Yes — comfortably cool in summer and warm in winter. Cyprus summers are no joke; we have planned for them.

items.q: Can I do Pilates while pregnant?
items.a: In many cases yes, with the right guidance. Our instructors are fully certified in pre-natal movement. We recommend private sessions during pregnancy so everything is tailored to you — and always check with your doctor first.

items.q: When can I return after giving birth?
items.a: Every recovery is different. With your doctor's clearance — typically from six weeks after birth — our post-natal certified instructors will rebuild your strength gradually and safely, starting with the deep core.

items.q: I have back pain. Is reformer Pilates safe for me?
items.a: Reformer Pilates is often recommended for back pain because the springs support you while you strengthen the muscles that protect your spine. Tell us about your pain when you book — we may suggest starting with a private session.

items.q: Can I train with an injury?
items.a: Often yes, and thoughtfully. Message us about your injury before booking. Private sessions let us work around and with your body; in group classes we offer modifications for most exercises.

items.q: Do you offer modifications in class?
items.a: Constantly. With six people maximum, your instructor adapts exercises to your level and any limitations in real time.

items.q: Is reformer Pilates safe for older adults?
items.a: Yes — the reformer is one of the most joint-friendly ways to build strength and balance at any age. Fundamentals is the right starting point.

items.q: Should I eat before class?
items.a: Keep it light. A small snack an hour or two before is ideal; a full meal right before class is not your friend on the reformer.

items.q: Do I need to tell you about health conditions?
items.a: Please do — it stays confidential and it helps us keep you safe. There is space for this when you register, and you can always message us privately.

items.q: How much does a class cost?
items.a: A drop-in class is €20. Packs bring the per-class price down to as low as €20 for groups, and monthly memberships run from €120. The intro pack gives newcomers two classes for €32. Full details are on our pricing page.

items.q: Do class packs expire?
items.a: Flexi packs are valid for 2 months (5 classes) or 3 months (10 classes). Monthly memberships renew monthly.

items.q: Can I share my pack with someone else?
items.a: Packs are personal. Friends are always welcome to join you with their own drop-in or intro pack.

items.q: What payment methods do you accept?
items.a: Card and cash at the studio, and card online once booking opens.

items.q: Is there a refund policy?
items.a: Unused, unexpired packs can be discussed case by case — talk to us. Completed classes and expired packs are non-refundable.

items.q: Are there founding member rates?
items.a: Yes — joining the founding member list before we open locks in exclusive rates and first access to bookings.

items.q: What language are classes taught in?
items.a: All classes are taught in English, and we welcome every nationality. Our team also speaks Greek.

items.q: Do I need to speak Greek to join?
items.a: Not at all. English is the language of the studio, and much of our community is international.

items.q: Can I come alone?
items.a: Most people do. Classes of six get friendly fast — coming alone is the normal way to arrive and rarely how people leave.

items.q: Is the studio beginner-friendly in atmosphere?
items.a: Completely. No mirrored walls of intimidation, no competitive energy. Chill vibes are found here — it is on the wall, and we mean it.
